newsitem.title: USA: Transport Corp adopts rights plan.
newsitem.headline: Transport Corp adopts rights plan.

text.p: Transport Corp of America Inc said Tuesday its board of directors has adopted a shareholder rights plan.
The company also said it was not aware of any current attempt to take control of the freight and logistics company.
The plan is designed to ensure that all of the company's shareholders receive fair and equal treatment in the event of any proposal to acquire the company, Transport Corp said.
The rights will be distributed for each share of common stock outstanding as of March 21, the company said.

The rights become exercisable only following the acquisition by a person or group, without the prior consent of the Transport Corp board, of 15 percent or more of the company's voting stock, or following the announcement of a tender offer or exchange offer to acquire an interest of 15 percent or more.
Rights owned by the acquiring person would become void, the company said.

"Transport America currently has no shareholder with an interest of 15 percent or more, and we are not aware of any current attempt to take control of the company," James Aronson, chief executive officer of Transport Corp, said in a news release. "The plan was adopted after extensive consideration by the board and is intended to protect the interests of our shareholders in the event of abusive or unfair takeover tactics."
Transport Corp shares were down 3/16 at 12 Tuesday.
